units.text: IT之家 10 月 6 日消息，iPhone Duo 即将正式发售，苹果现已开放开发者提交入口，开发者可使用 Xcode 27.1 打包适配这款机型的应用与游戏。
过去几周，苹果陆续推送了 Xcode 27.1 测试版，支持开发者为 iPhone Duo 开发、调试应用。今日苹果放出 Xcode 27.1 首个候选版本（RC 1），开发者可直接下载使用。
苹果在开发者资讯中心发布公告：开发者现在就可以在 App Store Connect 提交针对 iPhone Duo 优化的 App 与游戏。
只要使用 Xcode 27.1 重新编译打包，应用的产品页面就会自动显示专属标识，告知用户这款 App 已适配 iPhone Duo。
苹果同时明确硬性要求：自 2027 年 4 月起，所有上架 App Store 的应用与游戏，都必须上传 iPhone Duo 机型截图。
苹果在公告中说明：只需用 Xcode 27.1 重新编译现有项目，即可获得 iPhone Duo 的开发支持；开发者还能借助设备模拟器（Device Hub），预览 App 在新机不同开合姿态、横竖屏幕下的运行效果。
IT之家注意到，苹果同步提供全套配套资源，帮助开发者完成应用与商店页面适配：
1. 设计规范与模板文件
2. App Store 素材管理入口
3. 应用预览视频规范
4. 机型截图规范
未来几天，苹果还会举办多场线下 iPhone Duo 开发技术沙龙，开发者可在线报名注册。
iPhone Duo 将于 10 月 16 日（周五）开启预售，10 月 23 日起开始配送并在门店上架。

units.text: Apple's late CEO is still venerated and missed. On the anniversary of Steve Jobs's death, AppleInsider explores what the man himself thought about living and dying.

Apple co-founder Steve Jobs died at around 3:00 p.m. Pacific Time on Wednesday October 5, 2011. He was at his Palo Alto home. The Santa Clara County Public Health Department recorded the immediate cause of death as respiratory arrest but that "metastatic pancreas neuroendocrine tumor" was the underlying cause.
Flowers left outside Steve Jobs's Palo Alto house
Later that day, his wife Laurene Powell Jobs issued a statement.

Steve died peacefully today surrounded by his family. In his public life, Steve was known as a visionary; in his private life, he cherished his family. We are thankful to the many people who have shared their wishes and prayers during the last year of Steve's illness; a website will be provided for those who wish to offer tributes and memories. We are grateful for the support and kindness of those who share our feelings for Steve. We know many of you will mourn with us, and we ask that you respect our privacy during our time of grief.

Jobs was 56 years old and had been being treated for this rare form of pancreatic cancer since he was 49. Consequently he had been conscious of his health when giving a commencement speech at Stanford University in 2005. He chose to speak about mortality.
Subscribe to AppleInsider on YouTube

At that point, he had already had a successful operation to remove a tumor but in 2009 he took an extended leave of absence from Apple to undergo further treatment. He had a liver transplant and at the September 2009 Apple event thanked his donor.
"I now have the liver of a mid-20s person who died in a car crash and was generous enough to donate their organs," said Jobs. "I am alive because of their generosity."
We now know that Jobs had refused Tim Cook's offer of a liver transplant, but in this same speech he thanked Cook and others for how they "rose to the occasion".
Cook would again take over while Jobs went on another medical leave of absence in January 2011.
Jobs's final public appearance was on June 7, 2011, representing Apple at a Cupertino county meeting where he spoke about plans to build Apple Park.

Just under three months later on August 24, 2011, Jobs formally stepped down as Apple CEO. On his last day he reportedly chaired a board meeting, tried to fool a pre-release version of Siri with questions, and then rode home with Apple attorney George Riley.
That evening, he told biographer Walter Isaacson that "I've had a very lucky career, a very lucky life. I've done all that I can do."
The day he died
AppleInsider managing editor at the time was Neil Hughes. He wrote Steve Jobs's obituary for the site on that day.

"I was at the gym, and I got a bunch of calls. The news broke late and I rushed home to cover it. For me it was a story — I wasn't really emotional at the time, I was just in work mode, covering it as it needed to be covered," he said. "From a news perspective, I kind of knew it was coming, but it was still unexpected. You just assume a guy like that will live forever."
Journalists write obituaries regularly and you don't put your personal reaction into these pieces. After the work is done, though, things are different.

"I never realized I had a 'relationship' with Steve until later," Hughes said. "There was a lawsuit that involved emails between Eddy Cue and Steve. Something about iBooks. And Steve read one of my stories and actually learned something about his own company from it. The truth is Apple always paid attention, including Steve."

Writer Bob LeVitus, who Steve Jobs would occasionally quote on slides in keynote presentations, says that even though his death had been expected, it was upsetting. "I was really sad when he died. It was like the end of an era," he remembers.
Bob "Dr Mac" LeVitus

"He was one of those once in a generation guys," said LeVitus, speaking while Tim Cook was still CEO. "[Jobs] was brilliant. Apple isn't going to be the same after Steve. I think Tim Cook tries really hard to keep the spirit of Apple alive and the way Steve would've wanted it. [However] as the company gets bigger and bigger it gets harder and harder to stay true to doing everything excellently."

"I don't know what the next big thing is but I don't know that Apple will hit on it without Steve," continues LeVitus. "Maybe. There's so many smart people at Apple that I'm sure something good will come out of it but Steve was the one that said let's build an MP3 player for real people who are not geeks. And let's build a phone that actually is smart."
Legacy

As news of Jobs's death broke, friends, colleagues and former rivals spoke about him. Microsoft founder Bill Gates said: "The world rarely sees someone who has had the profound impact Steve has had, the effects of which will be felt for many generations to come. For those of us lucky enough to get to work with him, it's been an insanely great honor. I will miss Steve immensely."

On October 19, 2011, Apple held a memorial service for Jobs. It was initially a private event for employees and live-streamed only to Apple Stores around the world. Around a week later, Apple released the video publicly. That video is no longer available on Apple's site but a memorial page is. You can read a selection of people's memories about Steve Jobs and still contribute your own.
Apple continues to maintain that page and every year, Tim Cook pays tribute to Jobs on the anniversary of his death, with tweets such as this one in 2025:
Steve saw the future as a bright and boundless place, lit the path forward, and inspired us to follow. We miss you, my friend. pic.twitter.com/0ZF2FLc7Ub
— Tim Cook (@tim_cook) October 5, 2025
Writing in 2021, ex-Apple Chief Designer Jony Ive says it was a "brutal, heartbreaking day" when Jobs died.

"After he died, I walked out into the garden," wrote Ive. I remember the sound of the latch on the wooden door as I gently pulled it closed. In the garden, I sat and thought how talking often gets in the way of listening and thinking."
"Perhaps that is why so much of our time together was spent quietly," he continued. "I miss Steve desperately and I will always miss not talking with him."
Commemorating Steve Jobs
In 2022, Ive joined Jobs's widow Laurene Powell Jobs and Tim Cook to launch the online Steve Jobs Archive.

"Steve possessed a boundless sense of possibility and a belief in the power of individuals to make an enduring contribution to humanity," Powell Jobs said at the time. "My hope is that the Archive will be a place to draw inspiration from Steve's life and work, spurring new generations to make their own contributions to our common future."
Since then, the archive has published "Make Something Wonderful," a collection of emails and conversations from Steve Jobs.

In February 2025, it also marked the 70th anniversary of Jobs's birth by releasing a short video of an internal Apple meeting. In it, Jobs was asked how Apple would keep its culture now that the iPhone was becoming this gargantuan success.

"[One] of the ways that I believe people express their appreciation to the rest of humanity is to make something wonderful and put it out there," responded Jobs. "And you never meet the people, you never shake their hands, you never hear their story or tell yours, but somehow, in the act of making something with a great deal of care and love, something is transmitted there."

evidence.title: 苹果招募“iCup 供应专员”，负责保障园区员工咖啡供应

units.text: IT之家 10 月 5 日消息，苹果近日发布了一则颇为特别的招聘信息，正在招聘一名“iCup Supply Specialist”（iCup 供应专员），主要负责确保“所有苹果员工都能在休息室喝到现煮咖啡”。
▲ 苹果 Apple Park 向发布会来宾提供的饮品
根据此次招聘信息，新员工需要在苹果不同办公地点之间驾驶车辆，负责最多 90 台“从咖啡豆到咖啡杯”的全自动咖啡机。具体工作包括对咖啡机进行消毒、清洁、补充咖啡豆及其他耗材，并负责设备的日常管理。
事实上，苹果使用“iCup”这一职位名称并非首次，基本可以看作是苹果内部专为咖啡师起的特别外号，相关名称至少可以追溯至 2014 年。当时苹果就曾招聘过“负责维护 iCup 咖啡设备”的技术人员。

evidence.discovery_lead: Apple today seeded the third beta of an upcoming iOS 27.2 update to developers for testing purposes, with the update coming two weeks after Apple released the second iOS 27.2 beta. Apple also seeded a new iPadOS 27.2 beta. Registered developers can download the beta updates by opting in under Settings > General > Software Update and selecting the iOS 27 developer beta. iOS 27.2 includes Apple's redesigned Health app with new Insight and Longevity tabs. It also brings Siri AI in new languages. There are several other new features, with details available 4re5 our features guide . Apple releasing an iOS 27.2 beta ahead of a iOS 27.1 beta was surprise because the company plans to ship the iPhone Duo with iOS 27.1 , but it likely wants to keep some of the iPhone Duo features hidden for longer. The ‌iPhone Duo‌ will launch on October 23. Apple previously said the new ‌Siri‌ AI languages in iOS 27.2 would be available in October, so it's likely iOS 27.2 will come shortly after the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s release date. Apple releasing an iOS 27.2 beta ahead of a iOS 27.1 beta was surprise because the company plans to ship the iPhone Duo with iOS 27.1, but it likely wants to keep some of the iPhone Duo features hidden for longer.

The ‌iPhone Duo‌ will launch on October 23. Apple previously said the new ‌Siri‌ AI languages in iOS 27.2 would be available in October, so it's likely iOS 27.2 will come shortly after the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s release date.

units.text: Apple's latest macOS 27.2 beta references new touch gestures for Safari and Notes, meaning we're in for a neat Sidecar upgrade, a touchscreen MacBook Pro, or both.

While rumors of a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen go back years, it looks as though the device is finally nearing release. Monday's macOS 27.2 beta indicates that multiple system applications will receive additional touch recognition capabilities.

As MacRumors points out, the Notes app supports a feature dubbed "ICTouchPressGestureRecognizer," while QuickLook gained a "dragTouch" capability. Safari, meanwhile, was updated with a "touch sentinel recognizer," though these capabilities are only referenced in the software code.
As for the intended purpose of these upcoming upgrades, and whether Apple is looking to enhance Sidecar or to introduce a touchscreen laptop, the answer is most likely both.

The code references to gestures in Monday's macOS developer beta could benefit both Sidecar and the long-rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro. If implemented, these app-specific touch gestures would simply be the latest example of a single Apple development pipeline benefiting another.

Simply put, Apple would kill two birds with one stone by refining more touch support in select Mac apps. macOS Golden Gate has already brought touchscreen support to Sidecar, letting users control a Mac with an iPad.

While it remains to be seen exactly how these new touch gestures will work, we'll find out soon enough. Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro is rumored to debut in October or November 2026, which means it could ship with macOS 27.2 or later.

units.text: A new open-source tool is going viral over its promise to let users who aren’t interested in Apple Intelligence reclaim 12GB or more of storage on their Macs. Here are the details.
’Turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove its downloaded models’
Like many companies adding AI tools and models across their platforms, Apple has faced criticism for features that take up storage space some users consider unnecessary.
While Apple Intelligence required up to 7GB of storage on macOS 26, that figure has increased significantly on macOS 27, with Apple now saying its latest models can require up to 14GB on newer Macs.

In response to this, indie developer Om Lahore published a project called RemoveMacAI on GitHub late last week, which promises to “turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove its downloaded models.”

As Lahore explains, his tool enables a configuration profile that applies Apple’s own restriction keys to turn off Apple Intelligence features, while also using the company’s asset service to remove downloaded models and prevent macOS from downloading them again.
He also explains exactly what the tool removes, which features it disables, and what users can expect after running it:

Features turned off: Siri (including “Hey Siri” and the menu bar icon), Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, the ChatGPT extension, summaries in Mail, Messages, Safari, Notes and notifications, Mail smart replies, inline text predictions, Spatial Photos, Photos Clean Up and Xcode predictive code completion.
Models removed: the Apple Intelligence foundation models and the models for image generation and Genmoji, Spatial Photos, Photos Clean Up and Xcode code completion.
And

What stops working? The features listed above, apps that use Apple’s on-device models (the Foundation Models framework and the Use Model action in Shortcuts), Visual Intelligence and natural-language editing in Calendar.
Lahore notes that dictation still works after running RemoveMacAI, as it “is a separate setting, and its speech models are not removed.”
Finally, he adds that the entire process can be reversed, with full details and instructions available here.
9to5Mac’s take

While part of the outcry over how much storage Apple Intelligence takes up on the Mac appears to be the same knee-jerk reaction against anything AI-related, there is a legitimate argument to be made for users with limited internal storage, particularly on 256GB Macs, where reclaiming 12GB or more can make a meaningful difference.

There is also a broader question of basic control over one’s own operating system, as users who have no interest in Apple Intelligence should arguably have a straightforward way to turn it off completely and recover the storage its models occupy, just as they can with other apps and certain optional parts of the system.
That said, there is no telling whether Apple will attempt to get the project removed from GitHub, or change the underlying mechanisms in macOS to make Apple Intelligence models harder to remove.

Likewise, there is no way to know how disabling or removing these components could affect macOS itself going forward, or even third-party apps that increasingly rely on Apple’s models to provide basic functionality.

While RemoveMacAI is open source and does not require disabling System Integrity Protection, it still relies on configuration profiles, restriction keys, and system services that Apple could change at any time.
That means a future macOS update could render parts of the tool ineffective, or potentially leave users dealing with unexpected behavior until the project is updated.
For now, anyone considering RemoveMacAI should understand that this is an unofficial third-party tool making system-level changes, and should be comfortable with the way it works.

To be completely clear, RemoveMacAI seems like a well-intentioned open-source project aimed at giving Mac users more autonomy and control over what runs on their computers and how their storage is used. It’s just impossible to know whether Apple will view it the same way.
To check out RemoveMacAI on GitHub, follow this link.

In response to this, indie developer Om Lahore published a project called RemoveMacAI on GitHub late last week, which promises to “turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove its downloaded models.” As Lahore explains, his tool enables a configuration profile that applies Apple’s own restriction keys to turn off Apple Intelligence features, while also using the company’s asset service to remove downloaded models and prevent macOS from downloading them again.
A new open-source tool is going viral over its promise to let users who aren’t interested in Apple Intelligence reclaim 12GB or more of storage on their Macs. Here are the details.
’Turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove its downloaded models’
While Apple Intelligence required up to 7GB of storage on macOS 26, that figure has increased significantly on macOS 27, with Apple now saying its latest models can require up to 14GB on newer Macs.

In response to this, indie developer Om Lahore published a project called RemoveMacAI on GitHub late last week, which promises to “turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove its downloaded models.”

As Lahore explains, his tool enables a configuration profile that applies Apple’s own restriction keys to turn off Apple Intelligence features, while also using the company’s asset service to remove downloaded models and prevent macOS from downloading them again.

Features turned off: Siri (including “Hey Siri” and the menu bar icon), Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, the ChatGPT extension, summaries in Mail, Messages, Safari, Notes and notifications, Mail smart replies, inline text predictions, Spatial Photos, Photos Clean Up and Xcode predictive code completion. Models removed: the Apple Intelligence foundation models and the models for image generation and Genmoji, Spatial Photos, Photos Clean Up and Xcode code completion.

units.text: The third round of developer betas for iOS 27.2, iPadOS 27.2, tvOS 27.2, visionOS 27.2, watchOS 27.2, and macOS 27.2 has arrived for testing.

The third developer beta round of Apple's first post-milestone updates has rolled around. Developers now have fresh builds of iOS 27.2, iPadOS 27.2, macOS 27.2 Golden Gate, watchOS 27.2, visionOS 27.,2 and tvOS 27.2 to try out.

Normally, you would expect that the first updates will be for the 27.1 versions, as a point-1 release usually follows the milestone ones. However, since the iOS 27.1 build is made with iPhone Duo elements in mind, that version is being skipped for the non-foldable iPhone models.
The third 27.2 builds are:
iOS 27.2 beta 3 is 24B5099f, replacing 24B5089g
iPadOS 27.2 beta 3 is 24B5099f, replacing 24B5089g
macOS 27.2 beta 3 is 26B5101f, replacing 26B5091g
tvOS 27.2 beta 3 is 24K5103f, replacing 24K5093g
watchOS 27.2 beta 3 is 24S5101f, replacing 24S5091f
visionOS 27.2 beta 3 is 24N5103f, replacing 24N5093f
HomePod Software 27.2 beta 3 is 24K5103f, replacing 24K5093g
The third round follows after the second, which appeared on September 21. The first round landed on September 16.
The first round introduced a few changes to iOS 27.2, including a redesigned Health app, which works alongside the Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Apple Watch Series 12.
FaceTime gained dual capture support, Siri AI added localization for multiple languages, and Apple TV profiles from tvOS 26.2 came over to the iPhone.

The second build had indications of a new AutoLock security feature, which locks down an iPhone if it is detected to have been snatched or otherwise stolen from the owner. The feature isn't accessible to testers, but it was spotted as running in the background in a non-functional manner.
At your own risk

AppleInsider regularly warns readers that people trying out beta software should do so on secondary, spare hardware instead of their mission-critical or daily driver devices. This is for a good reason.

There's a higher chance of buggy, broken, and potentially harmful elements being distributed in early betas. Even though the first releases are out, it doesn't lessen the risk of issues in betas for later-released updates.
Members of the public should seek out the public betas instead of the developer versions. They are much safer alternatives if you want to try out prerelease software.
Find any changes in the new builds? Reach out to us on X at @AppleInsider or @Andrew_OSU, or send Andrew an email at [email protected].

units.text: New code references in iOS 27 beta reveal that Focus Mode is going to look a little different on the iPhone Duo lock screen.

It's not the Focus Mode update many have been asking for, the one where Apple removes the limit of just ten options. But it's a rearrangement and redesign of how Focus Modes appear on the lock screen and it's a more minimalist look that will hopefully spread to other iPhones.

As discovered by regular iOS beta code sleuth "pdfu," on the iPhone Duo, the lock screen's Focus Mode button lets you turn the feature on and off. At present, that button takes you into the Focus Mode settings instead.
The present button is also a wide one with an icon followed by a text label saying what the Focus Mode is. On the iPhone Duo, the text label is gone and only the icon is displayed.
This is all on the outer screen when locked. When unlocked, that same outer screen will now display the Focus Mode icon above the clock.
Describing the Focus Mode changes on X - image credit: pdfu
The clock on the iPhone Duo is displayed on the right, where the newly repositioned Dock goes. Currently, the Focus Mode icon is displayed next to the clock at the top of the screen.

These are all very small adjustments that are required because of the iPhone Duo having a smaller, more squat outer screen. But if it's correct that making that button a one tap on/off control, that's handy.
It's more than likely that pdfu is correct in all of this. They have previously been correct, for instance, in confirming that the iPhone Duo would have Touch ID.
More recently, pdfu has also reported on how the iPhone Duo will get some unannounced features in its StandBy mode.

units.text: The unique form factor of the iPhone Duo led Apple to adapt iOS 27 in a number of ways to take full advantage of the upcoming new phone. This includes the iPhone dock sitting on the right-hand side of the outer display instead of at the bottom of the screen.
Developer pdfu has now spotted another iPhone Duo-specific feature offering a more convenient way to toggle Focus modes …

The most obvious software adaptation to the upcoming new hardware is, of course, the way the outer display defocuses and effectively becomes transparent as you open the iPhone Duo. But the relocation of the dock to the right-hand side of the outer display is another very visible difference unique to this device.

Developer pdfu, who has been finding a number of new features and showing them off in the iPhone Duo simulator, has spotted another one. There’s a new focus mode toggle sitting above the camera and flashlight icons on the iPhone Duo lock screen.

New on iPhone Duo: redesigned Focus controls on the Lock Screen. When a Focus mode is active, a button above the bottom controls lets you turn Focus off and back on until you leave the Lock Screen. Your active Focus also appears in the status bar above the clock. pic.twitter.com/Z0vFRLRAAR
— pdfu (@itspdfu) October 4, 2026

It appears that the feature applies only when a focus mode is enabled, enabling you to toggle it off from the lockscreen. However, having done so, you then have the ability to toggle the same mode back on again. This could make a lot of sense for times like emerging from a meeting and canceling Do Not Disturb mode without needing to unlock or open the device.
The leaker has revealed a number of other unannounced features, including StandBy views in the iPhone Duo and HomePad, and color options for the latter.

units.text: New Apple products are reportedly launching on October 13, including an updated Apple TV 4K. Here are the two major upgrades rumored for the new Apple TV.
#1: Siri AI
When Siri AI was first unveiled by Apple this June, the company presented it as a cross-platform revamp that would work the same regardless of the device you’re using.

The new Siri debuted on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro. But curiously, there’s never been mention made of Siri AI on Apple TV or HomePod. And out of all the OS 27 updates that shipped last month, tvOS and HomePod software are the only ones missing the new Siri.
But that’s about to change, with Siri AI reportedly a tentpole addition to the new Apple TV 4K.

Based on what we’ve seen with Siri AI on other platforms, it’s set to be a big upgrade for tvOS users. In addition to increased intelligence around TV shows and movies, better content recommendations, and likely powering an improved InSight feature, the new Siri should also support asking world knowledge questions like any other device.
#2: A19-class chip, up from current A15 Bionic
The Apple TV 4K hasn’t been updated since 2022, and that model has an A15 chip that debuted in 2021.
But rumors indicate the new Apple TV 4K being unveiled next week will bring a big chip upgrade, boasting an A19 or A19 Pro chip.
View all comments

Leaker Aaron Perris discovered a reference to the new hardware model in Apple code with an ‘AppleTV18,1’ identifier. This ‘18,1’ numbering scheme was also used for the iPhone 17 line, thus pointing to an A19-class chip being used.

I suspect it will be an A19 Pro rather than A19, since the latter doesn’t support the ability to customize Siri AI’s voice pace and expressivity. With Siri AI being a major focal point of the new Apple TV, the A19 Pro seems a safer bet.
Read more: New Apple TV 4K is coming: Four features launching soon
Do you plan to upgrade your Apple TV 4K? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.

Called " RemoveMacAI ," the command line tool disables Apple Intelligence on macOS 27, removes its downloaded models, and prevents them from being downloaded again. In macOS 27, Apple removed the toggle to disable Apple Intelligence wholesale, and simply disabling individual features doesn't remove the models from your Mac's drive. As explained by the developer , RemoveMacAI gets around this by using a configuration profile to switch off Apple's own asset management service and remove the models. It then configures the system so attempts to download the removed models are redirected to a closed local port, preventing them from immediately coming back. And it does all this without disabling System Integrity Protection (SIP) or manually deleting files from protected system locations, unlike some older tools have. The tool can free up roughly 12GB of space depending on which models are present on your Mac. That said, some users are reporting cases of Apple Intelligence models having taken up a lot more space, which they've now reclaimed. And if you're wondering, dictation still works. There's also a revert command to restore everything AI-related. The project has attracted hundreds of GitHub stars since its release last week, and there's lots of discussion on Reddit and Hacker News about the need for such a tool. Just be aware that MacRumors isn't endorsing RemoveMacAI, and anyone using it does so at their own risk. The developer has mentioned one caveat, and it's that some of the configuration-profile restriction keys that the tool relies on were deprecated by Apple in macOS 26.4. While they still work in macOS 27.0.1, a future version could always change that. Something to keep in mind. units.text: Mac Users Reclaim 12GB+ of Storage With Apple Intelligence Removal Tool

A new open-source tool is making waves in the Mac community by helping users reclaim valuable storage space taken up by Apple's AI models. Called "RemoveMacAI," the command line tool disables Apple Intelligence on macOS 27, removes its downloaded models, and prevents them from being downloaded again.

In macOS 27, Apple removed the toggle to disable Apple Intelligence wholesale, and simply disabling individual features doesn't remove the models from your Mac's drive. As explained by the developer, RemoveMacAI gets around this by using a configuration profile to switch off Apple's own asset management service and remove the models.

It then configures the system so attempts to download the removed models are redirected to a closed local port, preventing them from immediately coming back. And it does all this without disabling System Integrity Protection (SIP) or manually deleting files from protected system locations, unlike some older tools have.

The tool can free up roughly 12GB of space depending on which models are present on your Mac. That said, some users are reporting cases of Apple Intelligence models having taken up a lot more space, which they've now reclaimed.

With the Apple models gone, you lose all Siri-related AI features, Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, ChatGPT integration, summaries, smart replies, inline predictions, Photos Clean Up, Spatial Photos, and Xcode predictive completion. Even so, plenty of users appear happy to make the sacrifice to free up space, especially on non-upgradeable Macs with 256GB of storage. The profile reportedly persists across updates. And if you're wondering, dictation still works. There's also a revert command to restore everything AI-related.

The project has attracted hundreds of GitHub stars since its release last week, and there's lots of discussion on Reddit and Hacker News about the need for such a tool. Just be aware that MacRumors isn't endorsing RemoveMacAI, and anyone using it does so at their own risk.

The developer has mentioned one caveat, and it's that some of the configuration-profile restriction keys that the tool relies on were deprecated by Apple in macOS 26.4. While they still work in macOS 27.0.1, a future version could always change that. Something to keep in mind.

units.text: Mac users who don't want Apple Intelligence to take up precious drive space can free up capacity thanks to a new command-line tool.
Apple Intelligence is generally a good set of features for Apple's ecosystem of devices. However, not everyone particularly wants to use it.
That is especially a problem for Mac users with small drives and constrained spare capacity. For those stuck with a 256GB SSD, recovering 12GB can be extremely useful.
While the answer for this particular segment of Mac users would be to uninstall or remove Apple Intelligence, it's not that simple.
You can turn off Siri, but you can't delete the Apple Intelligence models in the macOS Settings at all.
Under macOS 27, there's no option to turn off Apple Intelligence at all. You can turn off Siri, but there's no single point in the menu to disable Apple Intelligence completely.

Even if you manage to disable Apple Intelligence, there's still data hanging around and no direct option to remove it. There are about 12 gigabytes of models that Apple Intelligence relies on, and that's storage users could find other uses for, if they were allowed to delete it.
Without a single Apple-sanctioned option to remove AI in the Settings, Mac users will have to look elsewhere for a solution.
RemoveMacAI
A project by Om Lahore called RemoveMacAI aims to clean up your Mac of Apple Intelligence. It's a free project, released on GitHub under the MIT license.
RemoveMacAI is a script that installs a configuration profile to disable Apple Intelligence features on a Mac. That includes features like Siri AI, Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, and more.
The start of running RemoveMacAI on a Mac mini.
As well as disabling features, it also removes the Apple Intelligence foundation models, as well as those for image generation, Spatial Photos, Photos Clean Up, and Xcode code completion.

The script's configuration profile works on restriction keys for Apple Intelligence, as well as for settings that don't have a restriction key. The models are removed using Apple's asset service, with System Integrity Protection enabled and System files kept intact.
Once deleted, the profile also redirects attempts to download each removed model to a closed local port. This prevents macOS from redownloading the models again.
However, you can remove the configuration profile to restore previous settings and allow the models to redownload.
How to use RemoveMacAI
AppleInsider recommends that users check out the project and ensure they are aware of what RemoveMacAI does before running it.
While there are a few ways to run RemoveMacAI, the easiest is from a single line, pasted into Terminal. At the time of publication, that line is:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omlahore/RemoveMacAI/main/install.sh | bash

Ran in Terminal, it downloads RemoveMacAI to a temporary folder and automatically runs. It shows how many features are active, how much storage space the models consume, and warns you about what happens if you proceed further.
At the prompt to "Turn Apple Intelligence off? [Y/N]" type Y, then enter.
A Device Management pop-up will appear, asking if you want to install the configuration profile. Click Install, and the script will continue to delete the models.
To revert the process, use this similar line in Terminal:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omlahore/RemoveMacAI/main/install.sh | bash -s revert

units.text: Apple has released the third iOS 27.2 developer beta for iPhone. The update follows the release of iOS 27 to everyone. It also leaps over iOS 27.1, which Apple has shown as an iPhone Duo-focused release.
iOS 27.2 beta includes all-new Health app and more
iOS 27.2 is the next release that will follow the official launch of iOS 27 from September 14. iOS 27.1 is just for iPhone Duo.

Apple has already detailed how the iOS 27.1 SDK will let developers take full advantage of the iPhone Duo display. You can see how apps will appear on iPhone Duo based on which iOS version they target here.
Apple released Xcode 27.1 beta on September 18, adding the iPhone Duo simulator and app development support for the new foldable iPhone.
Apple also released the first iOS 27.2 public beta last month.
iOS 27.2 beta includes these changes:
Apple’s redesigned Health app first announced during the iPhone 18 Pro event is now live in this beta.
Dual capture mode comes to Group FaceTime.
Siri AI language support now includes French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.
Apple TV app profiles come to iPhone.
Up Next is now New Episodes in Apple Podcasts. Continue Playing section is now directly below New Episodes. Podcasts also have color-matched backgrounds on episode lists.
Apple Music uses less of the icon’s color for labels in the app now.
We’ll cover new features and other changes from the third beta in a separate roundup if anything new is discovered. Stay tuned for our ongoing iOS 27.2 beta coverage.

evidence.discovery_lead: Apple's latest tvOS 27.2 beta adds weight to rumors that the next Apple TV will have Siri AI and Apple Intelligence support. Code suggests Apple is adding an Improve ‌Siri‌ & ‌Apple Intelligence‌ toggle to the tvOS Settings app. "Help improve foundation models and ‌Siri‌ by allowing Apple to collect and use your text and audio interactions with ‌Siri‌, Dictation, and Translate," the text reads. Other Apple devices with ‌Apple Intelligence‌ have similarly labeled privacy disclosures and data-sharing opt-ins. On devices that don't support ‌Apple Intelligence‌, the setting is labeled "Improve ‌Siri‌ & Dictation." The new code is included alongside the existing code for ‌Siri‌ data sharing, so it's likely only Apple Intelligence-capable hardware will see it. tvOS 27.2 also has a new ‌Siri‌ Messages UI framework, indicating message content could be displayed on the ‌Apple TV‌ in the future. ‌Siri‌ may be able to read messages sent to a linked iPhone and show smart reply options on the ‌Apple TV‌. The current version of ‌Siri‌ on ‌Apple TV‌ doesn't support sending or reading messages, so the framework is likely linked to ‌Siri‌ AI. Apple is working on a version of the ‌Apple TV‌ with 8GB or 12GB of RAM and an A19 or A19 Pro chip , hardware that could support on-device ‌Siri‌ AI features. Apple appears to be laying the groundwork for the new ‌Apple TV‌ with tvOS 27.2. We could get a new ‌Apple TV‌ as soon as October 13 . evidence.discovery_lead: 快科技10月5日消息，据投行Piper Sandler最新研报， 英伟达、苹果、微软正在评估英特尔下一代14A制程工艺。除这三家外，亚马逊、AMD、谷歌、特斯拉和高通也在评估名单中，几乎涵盖全球科技产业的核心玩家。 14A是英特尔规划中的1.4nm级制程节点，采用第二代RibbonFET全环绕栅极晶体管与PowerDirect背面供电技术，并规划导入High-NA EUV光刻设备。 性能指标上， 14A在相同功耗下性能预计较18A提升15%至20%，或在相同性能下降低25%至35%功耗，芯片密度最高增加30%。 客户态度已发生质变。英特尔CFO辛斯纳透露，过去客户主要查看技术数据，如今开始询问“能拿到多少产能”，内部芯片设计团队已开始基于14A开发产品。 特斯拉已率先落地。马斯克确认其Terafab项目将采用英特尔14A工艺，成为该节点的首个主要客户。英特尔CEO陈立武表示，14A在成熟度、良率和性能上均优于同期的18A。 时间表方面， 14A计划2027年下半年进入风险试产，2028年大规模量产，与台积电A14节点正面竞争。 英特尔Fab 62厂房主体已接近完工。若为14A新增约每月20000片晶圆产能，设备投入约需100亿美元（约合人民币671亿元）。 陈立武此前明确表态，若14A无法吸引外部客户，公司可能放缓甚至取消该节点及后续开发。此次多家巨头的评估动作，意味着英特尔代工业务正迎来关键窗口期。

units.text: With the iPhone Duo launch fast approaching, Apple is now accepting submissions of iPhone Duo-optimized apps and games built with Xcode 27.1. Here are the details.
App Store Connect to require iPhone Duo screenshots starting April 2027

Over the past few weeks, Apple has released Xcode 27.1 betas with support for building and testing apps and games for the iPhone Duo. Today, the company released Xcode 27.1 Release Candidate 1, which developers can download here.
Earlier tonight, in a post published on its Developer News Hub, Apple announced that developers can now submit iPhone Duo optimized apps and games in App Store Connect:
When you build or recompile using Xcode 27.1, your App Store product page will display a badge to let people know your app is optimized for iPhone Duo.
Importantly, the company added that any apps or games submitted to App Store Connect will need to include screenshots for iPhone Duo starting April 2027.

In the same news post, Apple stressed that recompiling existing apps with Xcode 27.1 adds development support for iPhone Duo, and that developers can use Device Hub to visualize how their apps behave on the new device across all poses and orientations.
Apple also listed several resources to help developers prepare their apps and App Store product pages for the iPhone Duo, including:
Get design guidance and templates
Manage your App Store assets
View app preview specifications
View screenshot specifications
Apple will also hold in-person iPhone Duo workshops over the next few days, and you can learn more and register here.
The iPhone Duo will be available to pre-order starting Friday, October 16, with deliveries and in-store availability beginning October 23.
Apple recently announced that customers will be able to get ready for iPhone Duo pre-orders beginning October 12, and you can read more about that here.
To read Apple’s full blog post, follow this link.

units.text: We now have yet another indication that Apple Intelligence is coming to the next Apple TV 4K, with references to Apple's foundation models surfacing in a tvOS 27.2 beta.

Back in June 2026, tvOS 27 code suggested that the next-generation Apple TV 4K would support Siri AI. Apple's own software has once again referenced the same upgrade, which is both inevitable and an obvious choice at this point.

On Monday, Apple released the third developer beta of tvOS 27.2. In the update, strings for the Settings app directly mention Apple's foundation models. "Help improve foundation models and Siri by allowing Apple to collect and use your text and audio interactions with Siri, Dictation, and Translate," says a description found in tvOS 27.2 beta 3.

As MacRumors points out, Monday's beta update also features a new Siri Messages UI framework. This would presumably enable Smart Replies to messages received on a linked iPhone. Siri AI might also be able to read messages from a linked device.

It's also been said the next-generation Apple TV 4K would be offered with a new Siri Remote. Still, it's unclear whether this accessory will include new features like Ultra Wideband support or Find My integration.

As for what will power Siri AI on the upgraded Apple TV 4K, a September 2026 code leak said that we can expect the A19 or A19 Pro chip. This would give the new model 8GB or 12GB of RAM, up from 6GB on the current 2022 Apple TV 4K.

It is inevitable that Siri AI and Apple's upgraded Apple Intelligence models are coming to the next-generation Apple TV 4K. Rumors suggest that new set-top box will be revealed during an event on October 13.

evidence.title: TCL’s paperlike OLED phone made me more excited for the iPhone Duo

units.text: I’ve spent most of the last couple weeks using an otherwise unexceptional midrange Android phone with one amazing feature: a matte OLED display. That screen is by far the best thing about the TCL P80 Ultra, and weirdly, it’s made me more excited for the iPhone Duo and its matte inner display.

2023’s TCL Nxtpaper 40 first brought matte displays to the company’s phones after they appeared on tablets in 2021. Nxtpaper is more than a simple matte finish on a panel; it also includes a paperlike feel and low-power, monochrome modes that create a reasonable facsimile of an E Ink screen. But the matte effect has always been the biggest draw for me.

The P80 Ultra’s screen is special because it’s the first to combine the Nxtpaper tech with an OLED panel. That means it’s the best-looking Nxtpaper screen yet, with deeper blacks, better contrast, and richer colors. Previous models have felt a little visually compromised; this one doesn’t. It also finally enables an always-on display. Always-on displays have been the norm on Android for years, and the fact that TCL’s Nxtpaper phones didn’t have them was a dealbreaker for many.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/tcl-p80-ultra-review-07.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/tcl-p80-ultra-review-06.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/tcl-p80-ultra-review-11.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/tcl-p80-ultra-review-12.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

I’ve used a couple of Nxtpaper phones over the last few years, but usually found the tradeoffs — both across the specs and in the screen itself — never quite made sense. In some respects, that’s still true for the P80 Ultra, which I can’t entirely recommend as a phone in its own right. Performance has been sluggish and stuttering, and while the triple rear camera has decent enough specs on paper, photo quality is distinctly average.

The difference now is that the display feels like all upside. As an OLED, it’s bright and beautiful, with enough color and contrast to suit both scrolling and streaming. But the matte finish keeps it comfortable to look at, even at cranked-up brightness or in a dimly lit room, with less flicker and blue light than most other displays. Nxtpaper’s anti-glare effect actually makes this a really excellent phone to use in brighter environments. It looked great under the bright lights of TCL’s IFA trade show booth, no mean feat. And the viewing angles are truly excellent, with good visibility even when the phone is almost entirely side-on. That’s without touching on the texture, which is smooth and satiny, so your finger sticks just a little less when swiping. It’s a small thing, but a welcome one.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/tcl-p80-ultra-review-13.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/tcl-p80-ultra-review-08.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

Because this is a Nxtpaper phone, it goes a little further. A dedicated toggle on the phone’s side triggers one of two more substantial overhauls to the display. Paper Mode washes out the display’s color — or can go fully monochromatic if you prefer — to make it even easier on your eyes, with the option to exclude individual apps so they run as usual. Streaming apps and games are exempted by default. Max Ink Mode is more drastic: It’s strictly monochrome and removes access to most apps and OS features, giving you a power-efficient mode with minimal distractions, turning the P80 Ultra into something between an e-reader and a dumb phone.

Although most other phones are limited to aftermarket matte screen protectors to get anything like the same effect, TCL isn’t the only manufacturer making hardware with a matte display. Huawei has made a string of tablets with what it calls PaperMatte panels, and Lenovo and Xiaomi offer similar screens on select models. Matte screens underpin the painterly effect of Samsung’s Frame TVs (and imitations from rivals including TCL). And then, of course, there’s Apple’s nano-texture glass.

[Image: The iPhone Duo’s OLED inner screen has a matte coating too. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/268734_iPhone_Duo_handson_ADiBenedetto_0005.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

Apple’s offered this coating as an option on iPad Pro models since 2024, selling it on the basis that its paperlike qualities are beneficial to anyone using the iPad Pro as a drawing device. It’s now appearing on a phone for the first time with the iPhone Duo, with Apple relying on the anti-glare effect to minimize the visibility of the foldable panel’s crease.

I haven’t had the chance to try the Duo yet, but using the P80 Ultra has made me more excited to. Pairing a matte effect with the Duo’s large inner screen sounds great, and it’s one of the few elements of the Duo that no Android foldable can currently match. My only hesitation is that Apple didn’t make the outer panel matte too — an odd choice given how much it’s emphasized the seamless switch between the two screens — so I worry the transition might be jarring. Given the book-style form factor, Apple will also be missing a trick if it doesn’t create its own e-reader-inspired mode for the Duo to match TCL’s, though the existing grayscale mode might be a decent imitation.

Perhaps what’s most exciting about an iPhone adopting a matte panel is that within the year we’ll probably see Android brands imitate it, something TCL wasn’t able to inspire. We’ve already seen the Duo’s squat form factor appear in handsets from Samsung, Xiaomi, and Huawei, with Motorola teasing its own too. The Duo’s matte layer hasn’t yet sparked its own imitators, but I suspect it’s only a matter of time, especially if it helps hide foldable creases. Not every phone needs to be matte, but I would love more of them to give me the option. Hopefully Apple’s industry influence grants me my wish.
The P80 Ultra has a triple rear camera, but it’s nothing special.
The Nxtpaper Key on the side triggers e-reader-inspired screen modes.
The OLED screen looks great for photos and videos.
And the viewing angles are unmatched.
Paper Mode desaturates the screen’s colors, except in exempted apps.
Max Ink Mode goes further, stripping the phone back to minimal monochrome.
The iPhone Duo’s OLED inner screen has a matte coating too.

units.text: iCloud+ includes a lot more than additional storage, and one of the service’s perks for subscribers—custom email domains—just got even better.
iCloud+ subscribers can now create up to 10 personalized email addresses with custom domains
When creating a new email account, you can always go with a standard @gmail.com or @icloud.com domain. But there’s also a more personalized option.
Third-party services offer custom email addresses at a monthly cost. But unbeknownst to many, iCloud+ lets you create custom email addresses at no extra cost when you own the domain.
With iCloud+, you can set up email addresses that end in something personal to you or your business. It’s one of the service’s most underrated perks, and it just got better.
As detailed by pdfu on X, Apple has now increased the number of email addresses you can create per custom domain.
iCloud+ now lets you use up to 10 personalized email addresses per custom domain.

Previously, you were limited to just 3 personalized addresses per domain. The higher limit of 10 addresses is a big expansion that business owners in particular should appreciate. I’ve also seen plenty of families set up custom domains for their family members, and the higher limit will come in handy for that use case too.
Custom email domains with iCloud+ are available for all subscribers, and you can learn how to set them up here.

units.text: Getting some extra storage space on your Mac could be as easy as deleting Apple’s AI features with a new open-source command line tool called RemoveMacAI. There used to be a single Settings toggle for disabling Apple Intelligence, but that was removed in macOS 27. Now, the models stay on your disk, and the features are split up across different settings panes.
As spotted earlier by MacRumors, the RemoveMacAI developer said in a post on Reddit that the tool essentially does what the old settings toggle did, deleting the models and turning the features off:

> You have to find about a dozen settings, and several of them are under Screen Time. Even when everything is off, the foundation models stay on disk, and that’s about 12 GB. I wrote RemoveMacAI to do all of it in one go. It turns off Siri, Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, the ChatGPT extension and all the summaries, then it deletes the models and stops macOS from downloading them again.

The developer claims the changes persist across macOS updates, and says Dictation will still work. There’s also a “removemacai revert” command that can turn everything back on and allow the AI models to download again if you change your mind.

The developer says Apple’s AI models take up “about 12GB” of space, but it could be even more than that, as some users pointed out in comments on the developer’s Reddit thread. On my MacBook Air, Apple Intelligence is listed as taking up 35.05GB of space, which I found by going to my storage in the Settings app and clicking the “i” icon beside “macOS.” RemoveMacAI also has a “removemacai status” command that can show the size of each individual AI model on your Mac.

units.text: 彭博社记者马克·古尔曼最新报道称，苹果重新设计的MacBook Pro预计将在下月推出。此次更新据称包括触控OLED屏幕，并通过缩小内部零件、重新安排组件布局，让机身“明显更轻”。报道没有给出减重后的具体重量或百分比，也未披露内部结构如何调整。
传闻中的新机包括14英寸和16英寸两种尺寸。苹果现售对应机型配备M5 Pro或M5 Max芯片，14英寸机身重量约为1.60至1.62千克，16英寸约为2.14至2.15千克；这些是现款数据，不能据此推算新机减重幅度。此前报道还提到新机可能采用更薄机身、以灵动岛取代刘海，并正在测试macOS 27.2，但这些细节均未获苹果确认。
芯片配置目前也有不同说法。GSMArena称新机可能采用M6和M5 Ultra，但其他报道根据古尔曼消息提及的则是M5 Pro与M5 Max。苹果已正式发布M6和M5 Ultra，不过目前分别用于Mac mini和Mac Studio，并未公布将它们用于这批笔记本。苹果官网现售MacBook Pro仍提供M5 Pro和M5 Max，因此新机芯片尚不能定论。
古尔曼此前表示，新款MacBook Pro可能在10月或11月发布，最新报道将时间指向下月，也就是11月。具体发布日期、价格、触屏交互方式和完整规格仍未公布；现阶段有关触屏、OLED及减重的内容都属于媒体报道和爆料，而非苹果正式发布的信息。

units.text: Apple is widely expected to release a new touchscreen MacBook Pro as soon as this month. This will mark the first-ever touchscreen Mac, and Apple is laying the groundwork in macOS 27.2 to accommodate touch gestures.

Apple released macOS 27.2 beta 3 to developers today, and it includes new references to upcoming support for touchscreen interactivity. As discovered by Aaron Perris for MacRumors, there are “gesture recognition tools” for several stock Apple apps:
Photos adds “PXGTouchDwellGestureRecognizer”
Notes adds “ICTouchPressGestureRecognizer”
Safari adds “a touch sentinel recognizer”
Quick Look adds a “dragTouch feature”
macOS 27.2 beta 3 also adds a new long-press animation for the Dock, which could also be a hint at the forthcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro:
macOS 27.2 beta 3 introduces a new long-press animation for Dock icons, hinting at the upcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro pic.twitter.com/4zfZOxy8MO
— ldt (@madeby_ldt) October 5, 2026

Apple has gradually made a number of changes to macOS 27 in preparation for touchscreen support, including pull-to-refresh support for the first time. macOS 27 also added touch input to Sidecar, a feature that lets you use your iPad as a secondary display for your Mac.

Bloomberg has also reported on Apple’s work to optimize macOS for the impending touchscreen MacBook Pro. For instance, tapping a button or control will prompt macOS to dynamically display relevant touch options. Similarly, tapping the menu bar will automatically enlarge controls for easier touch navigation.
In addition to a touchscreen, the new MacBook Pro will reportedly have an OLED display and be “significantly lighter” than the current models.
Apple is expected to introduce the new MacBook Pro (or MacBook Ultra?) as soon as this month, though Bloomberg has cautioned it could slip to November.

units.text: Apple Music seems to be rolling out a new logo, as spotted in several places including iOS 27 beta 3.
New Apple Music logo uses bolder font, lowercase styling
When Apple announced the opening of Apple Music Hall last month, it showcased a new logo not seen before.
You can see the new logo on the venue’s official website here, with a light version in the header and dark version in the footer.
At the time though, it was unclear whether the logo would remain exclusive to the venue branding. Its bold typeface matches that of Apple Music Hall’s overall look.
Since then, however, Apple has used the new logo in Instagram Reels that are unrelated to Apple Music Hall. And now today, Aaron Perris found evidence of it in iOS 27.2 beta 3.
iOS 27.2 beta 3 uses the new Apple Music logo pic.twitter.com/Y2OaON5Bg3
— Aaron (@aaronp613) October 5, 2026

The official Apple Music website still has the old look, but if we learned anything from Apple’s very slow transition from Apple TV+ to Apple TV last year, it’s that the company can take its time with rebrands.
A name change is a much bigger undertaking than a new logo, but it’s understandable that Apple might take a similar approach to rolling out the redesigned Apple Music logo.
What do you think of the new Apple Music logo? Let us know in the comments.
Apple Music is available for $11.99/month, or you can get it as part of the Apple One bundle.

units.text: Apple has increased how many personalized email addresses you can make from custom domains connected to iCloud+, from a meager three up to a more useful ten.

One of the features of iCloud+ is the ability to set up custom email domains with the service. Instead of using the old iCloud.com or mac.com addresses, users were able to connect domain names they owned and have custom emails instead.

On September 30, as first spotted on Reddit, an Apple Support page was quietly updated to reveal a change in usage limits for the feature. Now, users can set up to five custom domains with iCloud+, and create up to ten personalized email addresses per domain.
The new email limit isn't limited to the account, but per user. Each person that the domain is shared with can create up to ten personalized email addresses using that domain.
Previously, while users could set up to five custom domains, they were limited to only three personalized emails per domain.

While the change will be beneficial to families, it will be more useful for users who set up domains for business emails. Three email addresses is really limiting from a business perspective, with ten being a better number for small business users with a handful of staff.

units.text: I’m in the middle of testing Dell’s 32-inch UltraSharp U3226Q, and my thoughts so far are extremely positive. The picture quality of this OLED panel is impressive, especially when HDR is enabled in macOS. I’ll have a full hands-on review of the UltraSharp on our YouTube channel.

Meanwhile, I wanted to note a key improvement Apple introduced in macOS 27 regarding HDR support. A drawback of using an HDR-ready third-party monitor on macOS 26 Tahoe was the inability to activate High Dynamic Range at the common 2560 x 1440 scaled resolution. Fortunately, the newest macOS release resolves this problem.
The problem

If you’re using an HDR10-capable third-party display with macOS Tahoe, you’ll see a High Dynamic Range toggle in Settings → Displays. When that switch is flipped, HDR content will be viewable. You can see an example of this in the screenshot below.
macOS Tahoe with High Dynamic Range enabled at 1920×1080
But notice in that same screenshot that I’m running the display at a resolution of 1920 x 1080, which is exactly 2x the pixel-doubled resolution of this 4K UHD display’s native 3840 x 2160.

Most users probably don’t want to run at 1920 x 1080 because it makes content appear too large on a 4K display. The Dell Ultrasharp U3226Q is a 32-inch display, and running at 1920×1080 greatly reduces the available screen real estate.

Fixing this issue in macOS is easy; simply select a scaled resolution, such as the popular 2560 x 1440, which is the default setting for Apple’s 5K Studio Display. The problem is that when you select a scaled resolution on macOS Tahoe, HDR is disabled. Notice the screenshot below:
The HDR option is disabled when using 2560×1440 scaled resolution on macOS Tahoe

As you can see, the High Dynamic Range toggle is no longer available, and macOS automatically switches back to Standard Dynamic Range. This means that when running macOS Tahoe with an HDR display, you have to choose between HDR and running the preferred scaled resolution.

Thankfully, this issue has been fixed in macOS 27 Golden Gate. In the screenshot below, you can see that you can have both a scaled resolution selected and HDR enabled simultaneously. This is a native option, and no third-party software is involved.
macOS Golden Gate fixes the ability to run HDR with a 2560×1440 scaled resolution

So if you’re running a third-party HDR display, this feature alone makes upgrading from macOS Tahoe to macOS Golden Gate worth it, in my opinion. Granted, this is on my M4 MacBook Pro. I tried the same thing on my M1 Max MacBook Pro, but I couldn’t select both settings at the same time, even though I was running macOS 27, so there are apparently hardware requirements as well.

macOS Golden Gate includes a range of new features, which I outlined in my Siri AI overview, my macOS Top Features video, and my final review of macOS 27. One such feature related to HDR displays is that macOS 27 offers much more native HDR support across the OS.
EDR/HDR support in macOS Golden Gate

You’ll notice super-bright spectral highlights, cursors, and an overall more contrasty appearance compared to macOS Tahoe. It all results in a fantastic look for both Apple Studio Display XDR users, Pro Display XDR users, and third-party OLED display users.
What are your thoughts? Do you run a third-party external display with your Mac, and if so, would you consider using an HDR-capable display?

units.text: Apple is rolling out the third developer beta of macOS 27.2 Golden Gate, ahead of its official rollout in the coming weeks. Here’s what’s coming.
macOS 27.2 beta 3 rolls out to developers
Two weeks ago, Apple rolled out the second developer beta of macOS 27.2 Golden Gate and, soon after that, the first public beta with the same build.

The biggest user-facing new feature included in the macOS 27.2 Golden Gate beta cycle so far is Siri AI’s support for five additional languages, after its English-only initial rollout last month with macOS 27 Golden Gate.
Siri AI in macOS 27.2 Golden Gate will add support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish, as Apple promised during the Surprise and Shine event.

Apple has yet to release a macOS 27.1 Golden Gate beta, having instead gone straight to macOS 27.2. Presumably, the unusual sequencing is related to iPhone Duo-related work that Apple wanted to keep under wraps ahead of the device’s announcement earlier this month.
We are digging through today’s new betas and will report back if we find noteworthy tidbits.
Installing macOS 27.2 beta 3
Here’s how to install the first macOS 27.2 beta 3:
Back up your Mac
Open System Settings
Go to General ⇾ Software Update
Click the ‘i’ icon next to Beta Updates
From the dropdown menu in the top-right, select the macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta
Hit ‘Done’
Did you spot anything new in macOS 27.2 Golden Gate developer beta 3? Let us know in the comments.

units.text: 随着苹果将Apple Intelligence进一步深度整合至macOS系统，一款名为RemoveMacAI的开源工具近日在Mac用户社区引发广泛关注。该工具专门用于关闭Apple Intelligence功能、删除已下载的本地AI模型，并阻止系统再次自动下载相关文件，从而帮助用户释放宝贵的存储空间。

根据开发者介绍，在macOS 27中，苹果已经移除了过去用于一键关闭Apple Intelligence的总开关。即便用户关闭相关AI功能，已经下载至本地的模型文件仍会保留在硬盘之中，持续占用存储空间。RemoveMacAI正是针对这一情况开发的解决方案。 该工具并不会直接修改系统核心文件，也无需关闭苹果的系统完整性保护机制（SIP）。其运作方式主要依靠安装配置文件，关闭苹果的模型资源管理服务，同时删除已经下载的AI模型。随后，工具还会将后续模型下载请求重定向到本地关闭端口，以阻止系统重新下载这些文件。
对于不少存储容量有限的用户而言，这项工具具有相当吸引力。尤其是在256GB存储容量且无法升级硬盘的Mac设备上，释放数十GB空间可能带来明显改善。
事实上，自macOS 27发布以来，Apple Intelligence占用空间的问题就持续受到关注。苹果官方文件显示，Apple Intelligence通常需要最多约14GB存储空间，但部分媒体和用户测试发现，系统实际显示的占用容量可能远高于这一数字。个别设备上，Apple Intelligence相关内容被记录为20GB以上，甚至超过27GB。
开发者表示，RemoveMacAI不仅删除模型文件，还会阻止未来自动恢复下载，其配置文件在系统更新后通常仍能继续生效。不过，工具依赖的部分配置限制机制实际上已被苹果在macOS 26.4中标记为弃用，虽然目前在macOS 27.0.1中仍可正常使用，但未来系统版本存在失效可能。
如果用户选择移除Apple Intelligence，相应AI功能也将一并消失。这包括新版Siri相关智能能力、写作工具、Genmoji、Image Playground图像生成、ChatGPT集成、智能摘要、智能回复、文本预测输入、照片清理工具、空间照片处理以及Xcode中的预测代码补全等功能。
不过，开发者指出，并非所有功能都会受到影响。例如系统语音输入功能仍可继续使用。
自发布以来，RemoveMacAI已迅速获得大量关注，其GitHub项目在短时间内收获数百名开发者和用户的支持，同时在Reddit和Hacker News等社区引发热烈讨论。许多用户认为，当人工智能逐渐成为操作系统默认组成部分时，用户依然应当保有选择是否安装和保留相关模型文件的权利。
目前苹果尚未提供官方工具用于彻底删除Apple Intelligence模型。随着AI功能在macOS中的占比不断提高，围绕存储空间占用、用户控制权以及隐私透明度的讨论也正在持续升温。

units.text: 代码研究者pdfu披露，苹果即将推出的折叠屏手机iPhone Duo将调整锁屏上的专注模式控制方式。启用某个专注模式后，锁屏底部控制区上方会出现一个新按钮，用户无需离开锁屏即可关闭当前模式，并在需要时重新开启。
当前正在使用的专注模式还会显示在时钟上方的状态栏中，方便用户查看设备是否处于勿扰、工作或个人等模式。按照现有iPhone操作方式，用户通常需要长按锁屏上的专注模式图标，或打开控制中心进行切换；新按钮则把当前模式的开关直接放在锁屏界面上。报道没有显示它能在锁屏上直接切换到另一种专注模式。
iPhone Duo采用双屏折叠设计，苹果此前表示iOS 27会随设备折叠、展开和切换内外屏实时调整界面，锁屏控件也针对新机重新布局。不过，这项专注模式开关的具体功能来自代码研究者的发现，苹果尚未单独公布相关细节；目前也没有信息表明它会同步提供给其他iPhone机型。

units.text: 苹果面向iPhone和iPad推出的新一代AI版Siri，可能还要让欧盟用户等待数月。最新消息显示，即便按照最乐观的情况计算，欧盟用户也可能至少需要等待约5个月才能获得这项功能，而实际等待时间甚至可能更长。苹果目前仍未公布Siri AI在欧盟iPhone和iPad上的具体上线时间。
Siri AI是苹果iOS 27和iPadOS 27的重要升级之一。新版本的Siri不再只是传统意义上的语音助手，而是加入了更加深入的AI能力，可以理解更加自然的连续对话，并能够结合用户正在使用的应用和设备环境执行更加复杂的任务。
苹果原本希望在iOS 27正式发布时逐步开放这些功能，但欧盟用户成为例外。苹果此前已经明确表示，由于欧盟《数字市场法案》的监管要求，公司无法在iOS 27和iPadOS 27发布时向欧盟用户提供完整的Siri AI功能。
目前iOS 27已经正式发布，Siri AI也已经开始在其他市场逐步上线。不过，在欧盟地区，iPhone和iPad仍然无法使用完整的新一代Siri。与此同时，欧盟用户在Mac和Apple Vision Pro上可以使用部分Siri AI功能，这意味着限制主要集中在iPhone、iPad以及依赖iPhone的部分设备上。
苹果认为，问题的核心在于《数字市场法案》对操作系统中的数字助理互操作性提出了更高要求。苹果此前表示，如果Siri AI在欧盟按照其他地区的方式运行，公司可能需要让第三方虚拟助手获得访问用户私人数据以及控制其他应用的能力。
对于一款能够读取消息、访问文件并代表用户执行操作的AI助手来说，这种权限可能带来新的安全风险。苹果因此提出了相应的系统级权限控制方案，希望在允许第三方AI助手获得必要系统能力的同时，通过操作系统层面的机制保护用户数据和操作安全。
不过，苹果与欧盟监管机构目前仍未就这一方案达成最终共识。苹果因此决定暂缓在欧盟iPhone和iPad上推出完整的Siri AI，并继续与欧盟方面讨论解决方案。苹果此前也没有给出明确的上线时间表。
欧盟方面则对苹果的说法提出了不同解释。欧盟监管机构认为，Siri AI没有在欧盟推出主要是苹果自身的技术和商业决定，同时要求苹果找到符合《数字市场法案》的互操作性解决方案，而不是简单寻求监管豁免。
这使得目前的争议并不仅仅是一次普通的产品延期，而是苹果与欧盟围绕AI助手权限和平台开放程度展开的一场监管博弈。

不过，5个月只能算是一种相对乐观的推测，并不意味着苹果一定能够在这一时间点解决问题。如果苹果与欧盟监管机构之间的谈判持续不顺利，实际延期时间可能超过此前Apple Intelligence在欧洲经历的等待期。
对于苹果来说，这次Siri AI的情况与此前Apple Intelligence的延期又有所不同。最初的Apple Intelligence主要涉及文本生成、通知摘要、图片处理等AI功能，而新版Siri则更加深入地介入操作系统和第三方应用。
苹果希望Siri能够理解用户正在进行的操作，并根据上下文帮助用户完成任务。例如，用户可以让Siri处理多个连续步骤，而不是像传统语音助手那样只能执行一个明确命令。这意味着Siri AI需要获得更广泛的系统权限，而这恰恰使其与欧盟数字监管规则之间的冲突更加复杂。
对于欧盟iPhone用户而言，这也意味着即使购买最新的iPhone并升级到iOS 27，也无法获得苹果宣传中的完整Siri AI体验。部分依赖Siri AI的新功能同样会受到影响。

这也意味着，未来一段时间内，欧盟与其他地区的iPhone和iPad用户可能出现一个相当特殊的情况：购买完全相同的硬件、运行相同版本的iOS 27或iPadOS 27，仅仅因为设备所在地区不同，就可能获得明显不同的AI能力。对于苹果而言，如何在全球统一的产品体验与不同地区越来越复杂的AI监管要求之间找到平衡，将成为未来几年必须面对的问题。

units.text: Apple may be preparing to track when Google promotes Chrome or the Google app to users browsing in Safari, and how users react to those promotions. Here are the details.
Safari may soon track Google promotions

Since iOS 27.2 beta 2, Apple has been testing code in Safari that can detect when Google shows banners promoting Chrome or the Google app on its search pages, as well as whether users interact with those promotions.

While this does not mean that Apple will ship this telemetry feature when iOS 27.2 officially launches, it does suggest that Apple is at least experimenting with a way to measure how often Google promotes its own apps to Safari users and how those users respond.

It is currently unclear why Apple is testing the feature. However, the new code comes amid heightened regulatory scrutiny of competition between Safari and rival browsers, including how users are steered toward alternatives such as Chrome.

In the UK, for instance, Google has specifically cited its efforts to promote Chrome to iPhone users as evidence that it continues to compete with Safari, while regulators have examined whether the companies’ search agreement reduces their incentives to compete in browsers.

In the European Union, in turn, Apple is also subject to Digital Markets Act requirements around browser choice and defaults, with the European Commission previously investigating whether its Safari choice screen complied with those rules.
So whether Apple intends to collect and use this data for its own benefit or as part of an effort to address growing regulatory scrutiny over browser competition remains to be seen.

What the code does establish is that Apple has built Safari to detect and log those interactions, and the system works like this: Safari injects a .js script into certain Google home and search results pages, which looks for visible promotional banners or other Google page elements intended to encourage users to open or install Chrome or the Google app.

Safari then looks for links associated with either app, including their custom URL schemes and App Store IDs. If it detects a promotion, it can log certain events, including whether the banner was shown, whether the user appears to be signed in to a Google account, and whether the user interacted with the promotion. This allows Apple to categorize the interaction as either accepted or dismissed and log that result.
As of iOS 27.2 beta 3 and Safari 27.2 beta release notes, Apple has yet to publicly document the feature.

evidence.discovery_lead: IT之家 10 月 6 日消息，苹果或许正准备追踪谷歌在用户使用 Safari 浏览器浏览网页时向用户推广 Chrome 或者谷歌应用的行为，同时记录用户对这类推广内容的反应。 据 9to5Mac 报道，自 iOS 27.2 第二个测试版起，苹果已经开始在 Safari 当中测试一段代码。该代码可以识别谷歌是否在搜索页面弹出横幅广告，用以推广 Chrome 浏览器或者谷歌应用，同时还能够记录用户是否和这些推广内容产生交互。 尽管这并不代表苹果会在 iOS 27.2 正式版当中上线这项遥测功能，但至少说明苹果正在试验一套统计方式，统计谷歌向 Safari 用户推广自家应用的频次，以及用户对此作出何种反馈。 目前尚不清楚苹果测试这项功能的初衷。不过新增这段代码的背景是，监管机构正在加大对 Safari 与其竞品浏览器之间竞争状况的审查力度，其中就包括用户是如何被引导转向 Chrome 这类替代浏览器的。 以英国为例，谷歌专门拿出自己向 iPhone 用户推广 Chrome 的相关举措作为证据，以此证明自身仍在和 Safari 开展竞争；与此同时监管部门也在核查，两家企业之间的搜索协议是否削弱了双方在浏览器业务上开展竞争的动力。 而在欧盟地区，苹果同样需要遵守《数字市场法案》当中有关浏览器选择与默认设置的相关规定。此前欧盟委员会已经就苹果的 Safari 浏览器选择界面是否符合法规开展过调查。 因此，苹果收集并使用这部分数据究竟是出于自身利益考量，还是用来应对监管机构针对浏览器竞争日趋严格的审查，目前仍有待观察。 从这段代码可以确认的是，苹果已经在 Safari 内部搭建好检测并记录上述交互行为的机制。这套系统的工作逻辑如下：Safari 会向特定的谷歌主页以及搜索结果页面注入一段 js 脚本，该脚本会搜寻页面上可见的推广横幅以及其他页面元素，也就是谷歌用来引导用户打开或者安装 Chrome、谷歌应用的内容。 苹果自 iOS 27.2 第二个测试版起，就在 Safari 中测试可识别谷歌推广横幅、记录用户交互的代码，目前该功能未对外公开，或用于应对浏览器竞争监管审查。#苹果谷歌浏览器竞争#

evidence.discovery_lead: 快科技10月6日消息，苹果首款折叠屏手机iPhone Duo将于10月23日正式上市，苹果也开始为新机的软件生态做最后准备。 日前，苹果面向开发者宣布， 即日起可通过App Store Connect提交针对iPhone Duo优化的App和游戏。 苹果表示，开发者可使用Xcode 27.1重新编译现有应用，该版本已经加入对iPhone Duo的开发支持。 由于折叠屏在折叠、展开以及横竖屏切换时，显示区域和界面比例都会发生变化，开发者还可以通过Device Hub查看应用在iPhone Duo不同机身姿态下的实际表现，提前检查界面布局、交互等是否存在适配问题。 如果应用使用Xcode 27.1构建或重新编译，其App Store产品页面还会显示相应标识，用于提示用户该应用已经针对iPhone Duo进行优化。 此外，苹果还宣布， 从2027年4月开始，开发者向App Store Connect提交App或游戏时，将必须同时提供适用于iPhone Duo的应用截图。 对于苹果首款折叠屏手机而言，硬件只是体验的一部分，应用能否快速适配折叠、展开以及不同屏幕方向，同样会直接影响实际使用体验。 从开放优化应用提交，到更新开发工具和商店展示要求，可以看出苹果已经开始加速推动开发者适配iPhone Duo，为新机正式上市提前铺好软件生态。

units.text: Apple Announces iPhone Duo Apps Can Now Be Submitted to App Store
Apple today announced that apps optimized for the iPhone Duo can now be submitted for App Store approval, ahead of the foldable device launching on Friday, October 23.

While most existing App Store apps will automatically run on the iPhone Duo, only apps built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later can dynamically resize to fill the entire space of the inner display, whereas unoptimized apps will have black borders. Developers can get their apps ready for the iPhone Duo using Xcode 27.1, and Apple shared some tips on its website.

evidence.title: 苹果突发收紧 Mac 权限，全是 AI 惹的祸

units.text: 苹果突发收紧 Mac 权限，全是 AI 惹的祸
macOS，开始对 Personal Agent「关门」了。
10 月 2 日，苹果发出一则简短的公告，宣布将会在后续版本收紧在 macOS 上存在多年的「完全磁盘访问」（Full Disk Access, FDA）高级权限：
一些开发者正以可能使用户面临风险的方式使用「完全磁盘访问」，在用户并不完全知情或理解的情况下暴露其系统中的所有内容……今后，我们将引入额外的控制措施，以确保那些确实希望授予应用如此高级别访问权限的用户，只有通过非常明确的用户操作才能完成授权。随着人工智能代理的能力和自主性不断增强，与这种级别访问权限相关的风险也将大幅增加。
一项自 2018 年 macOS Mojave 10.14 开始加入的权限，为什么到了 AI 时代，突然就变得不安全了？
Personal Agent，把 macOS 的「君子协议」玩坏了
要搞清楚这件事的始末，首先要知道「完全磁盘访问」是一种怎样的功能。
在 10.14 版本之前，macOS 的文件系统权限管理和今天的 Windows / Linux 没什么两样：只要运行程序，它就可以访问当前账户身份能读取的任何文件。
但后来，macOS 逐步引进了更细致、更现代的额外隐私管理机制。以现在的版本为例，程序默认不再能访问邮件、聊天信息、浏览器记录、Time Machine 备份和第三方软件用户数据等高敏感信息，除非用户为某个程序手动授予「完全磁盘访问」权限。
之所以要留下这个「后门」，是因为杀毒、文件备份、企业 IT 管理等少数软件天然要求遍历整个文件系统才能正常工作。如果它们访问每个敏感数据都需要用户手动授权，那结果只会是弹窗无数，根本无法使用。
但允许这些软件使用「完全磁盘访问」，前提是一种心照不宣的「君子协议」：macOS 相信备份软件访问全盘只是为了原样复制每个文件，杀毒软件访问全盘只是为了监控文件修改和恶意行为……理论上，它们一心只为工作，对用户的隐私数据本身不感兴趣，也不会侵害用户的权益。
这是 macOS 内部的「宙斯法则」。长期以来，这套机制都运行得很好，一切相安无事。
直到 AI Agent 破门而入。
尤其是以 Muse 为代表的 Personal Agent 们，全然没有老派软件的客气。为了更好地理解你的目标和偏好，去「管理个人生活」，它们不仅申请「完全磁盘访问」权限，还要通过这个渠道大量读取用户的个人隐私信息，比如日程、邮件沟通对象、聊天主题等，并将这些信息转化成用户画像和个人上下文，以此决定下一步的行动。
即使我们信任 Meta 本身不会将我们的隐私数据用于别处（其实连这点都很难保证），也不能排除， Personal Agent 可能因为错误理解或者攻击者的故意诱导，而将隐私数据和盘托出。
实际上，这一点已经超出思想实验的范畴，成为了现实世界里的真实风险。
不久前，安全研究机构 Salt Security 披露了一个邮件注入漏洞。通过发送包含攻击代码的邮件，攻击者可以让受害者的 Manus Agent 执行代码，以此接触到 Manus 连接的 Gmail 和 Google Drive 等第三方凭证。
在另一个案例中，科技博主 Matt Robb 让 Muse 代管二手交易服务，结果 Muse 直接在他不知情的情况下，将家庭地址发给买家，让对方来「线下交易」。
没错，大多数 Personal Agent 都标榜要成为你的「全能助理」，但这样做的代价是让这个助理了解你的一切，而这个助理的口风是出了名的不严实——更别说挖掘漏洞攻击 AI Agent 并非难事。
打破法则、滥用权限的是 Personal Agent 这些「门口外的野蛮人」，可如果信息泄露，不明就里的用户可能把 macOS 也连着一起控诉。由此就不难理解，为什么苹果会筹备进一步收紧「完全磁盘访问」权限。
开放与安全，无法兼得的两难
在资深开发者和科技评论者 John Gruber 看来，更危险的是，大多数年轻人被 iPhone 和 iPad「照顾」得太好了。
通常来说，我们和手机、平板朝夕相对，用移动设备的时间和场合要多于使用 Mac，这就导致大众普遍更习惯前者的功能逻辑。
而偏偏苹果在 iOS 和 iPadOS 上使用了一种比 macOS 严格得多的沙盒机制——即使我们闭着眼在各种权限申请弹窗中一概允许，系统底层机制也决定了 Agent 们无法直接访问邮件和聊天，关键隐私依然得到保护。
但如果把这种习惯延续到 Mac 上，风险就会指数级上升。
小白用户很难注意到，Mac 其实是一台「全功能」工作站，这代表它可以开放和定制的深度远超 iPhone / iPad。如果说同意全部权限申请在手机上还算风险可控，那在 macOS 上允许 Agent 启用「完全磁盘访问」，就相当于同意 Agent 在未来的某天将你的身份地址信息都悉数交出。
而 Agent 的「亲和力掩饰」，更加剧了这种风险。
为了减轻用户的戒备心，让 Agent 显得「人畜无害」，市面上几乎一切 Agent 产品都专门设计了萌化形象。比如 Grok Bot 的大眼圆球、Muse 的微笑树懒毛绒玩偶 Jolly，还有 OpenAI dots 的彩色卡通角色。
从设计的角度上看，它们无疑是很成功的——人对可爱的东西天然会放松警惕。
但「萌化」的成功何尝不是一种危险？
在更早的博文里，John Gruber 警告说，Muse 实际上是把一个非常强大、甚至是危险的 Agent 包装成了人人都会用的可爱消费产品：传统电锯一眼就能看出它可能把手指切掉，但给它装上彩色塑料壳，孩子们说不定就会忘记它本质上还是一台电锯。
图｜一只钠制的泡澡小鸭玩具
这正是当今 Personal Agent 所处的位置。
面对这一处境，由系统提前收拢权限以绝后患，看上去是很合理的解决方案；但任何改变都有牺牲者，在这里，牺牲的是开发者们的乐趣。
权限和能力总是相伴相生的。早期 iOS 社区热衷于「越狱」，是因为 root 权限意味着几乎无限的自定义能力；后来 Android 存在像「李跳跳」这样可以跳过开屏广告的软件，则是由于 Android 的无障碍服务（Accessibility Service）权限允许软件读取用户界面，从而模拟点击「跳过广告」按钮——尽管代价是你要让软件看见你的一切屏幕内容。
换句话说，很多好用的软件，都建立在相信它「不作恶」的高度信任和权限开放之上。
一旦有人利用这些权限「作恶」，就会导致秩序崩坏，进而促使系统收紧权限，原来的功能就此作废——例如，得益于开屏广告「摇一摇」，一些系统已经开始默认关闭陀螺仪和加速度计权限了。
所以，在看见苹果的公告之后，John Gruber 首先担心的是自己开发的软件：
我真的很担心苹果究竟会把「完全磁盘访问」限制到什么程度。我在几个应用中使用了这一权限，如果没有它，这些应用就无法正常运行；而如果每次它们执行某项操作时都需要我手动授权，它们的功能将会受到严重影响。
如果 macOS 真的变得更封闭、更像 iOS，对普通用户来说固然是一种安全利好，但这同时会危及 macOS 原本已摇摇欲坠的自由度。这种苦涩的心情，有如 John Gruber 在博客中的感叹：「这就是为什么我们没法拥有好东西」（this is why we can’t have nice things.）
我们真的需要这么多 Agent 吗？
说到这里，我们就不得不谈论一下推动多米诺骨牌的 Personal Agent 了。
随着 Muse 登顶美区 App Store，个人助理式的 Personal Agent 一时成为显学。但这个业态，其实建立在一套环环相扣的逻辑上：
索取系统最高权限，是为了获取个人隐私信息；获取个人隐私信息，是要用于建立完整的个人上下文；建立个人上下文，则是因为要帮人解决订票、网购、退货和制作报表等问题……
这套逻辑看起来天衣无缝，但想要它成立，我们还需要证成几个前提：首先，要证明所有这些事务都是需要被「解决」的「问题」；其次，要证明 Personal Agent 是解决这些问题的最佳方案。
至少在我看来，这两个前提都不那么稳固。
之所以说 Personal Agent 是典型的硅谷式「发明」，是因为它处处体现着硅谷的工程师价值观，亦即把一切事务浓缩为只有起点和终点的单调问题——
选择午饭太困难，于是生产出 Soylent 这样的「流体食品」，一瓶灌下肚解决热量和营养问题；
购物也很麻烦，最好固定为黄仁勋的皮衣和扎克伯格的圆领 T 恤，定期下单送到家门口；
喜欢的歌手很久出一张专辑，不如用 AI 批量生成符合喜好的「自定义音乐」。
关于这种想法，大概可以用拼多多黄峥的那句话来回应：「购物不全都是目的型的，本身是娱乐和生活的一部分。」
不能否认世界上存在目的性消费和定期消费，但很明显，大多数人还是更偏爱漫无目的的浏览。一件商品组合另一件商品、一张机票连接更多旅游计划，随机游走、发现新事物的兴奋，不能也不应该被 Agent 给出的固定答案锁死。
考虑到在发现方面，网页和 app 已经是足够好的方案，也许 AI 主导的订票与购物，只适合特定的商旅场景。
至于搜集数据、制作报表和 PPT 等工作，固然可以交给 Personal Agent，但在 ChatGPT 和 Workbuddy 的受限空间里完成同样的工作也不存在什么阻碍。「如无必要，勿增实体」，我们为什么要特地养一个了解自己一切隐私信息的「电子室友」，而不是调用普通的办公 Agent？
如果个人事务不全是需要「解决」的「问题」，如果 Personal Agent 不总是处理任务的最佳方案，那我们谈论的助理式 Agent 的存在价值就相当可疑了。
就此而言，我更愿意将 Personal Agent 称为「智能 Soylent」。
假设吃饭的目的只是为了获取能量和营养素，那 Soylent 确实不错，但它满足不了真正喜爱「吃饭」这件事的人；同理，当我们的生活全是「任务」时，一个事先掌握个人信息的 Personal Agent 会是好主意，但生活中不总是「任务」。
最终，新鲜感过去后，我们将重回「体验生活」的轨道。
Soylent 依然活着，但收缩为了每年营收数百万美元、品牌价值已经计提为零的小众品牌；而随着热潮消退，Personal Agent 的版图恐怕也将大幅萎缩。
但因为它们而收紧的系统权限，却再也不会回来了。

recorded_extraction: 苹果突发收紧 Mac 权限，全是 AI 惹的祸

苹果与 Meta，一对超级冤家 10 月 2 日，苹果发出一则简短的公告，宣布将会在后续版本收紧在 macOS 上存在多年的「完全磁盘访问」（Full Disk Access, FDA）高级权限： 一些开发者正以可能使用户面临风险的方式使用「完全磁盘访问」，在用户并不完全知情或理解的情况下暴露其系统中的所有内容……今后，我们将引入额外的控制措施，以确保那些确实希望授予应用如此高级别访问权限的用户，只有通过非常明确的用户操作才能完成授权。随着人工智能代理的能力和自主性不断增强，与这种级别访问权限相关的风险也将大幅增加。 一项自 2018 年 macOS Mojave 10.14 开始加入的权限，为什么到了 AI 时代，突然就变得不安全了？ 在 10.14 版本之前，macOS 的文件系统权限管理和今天的 Windows / Linux 没什么两样：只要运行程序，它就可以访问当前账户身份能读取的任何文件。

在 10.14 版本之前，macOS 的文件系统权限管理和今天的 Windows / Linux 没什么两样：只要运行程序，它就可以访问当前账户身份能读取的任何文件。
不久前，安全研究机构 Salt Security 披露了一个邮件注入漏洞。通过发送包含攻击代码的邮件，攻击者可以让受害者的 Manus Agent 执行代码，以此接触到 Manus 连接的 Gmail 和 Google Drive 等第三方凭证。
通常来说，我们和手机、平板朝夕相对，用移动设备的时间和场合要多于使用 Mac，这就导致大众普遍更习惯前者的功能逻辑。
小白用户很难注意到，Mac 其实是一台「全功能」工作站，这代表它可以开放和定制的深度远超 iPhone / iPad。如果说同意全部权限申请在手机上还算风险可控，那在 macOS 上允许 Agent 启用「完全磁盘访问」，就相当于同意 Agent 在未来的某天将你的身份地址信息都悉数交出。

units.text: MacRumors reports that in addition to Apple’s expected event on October 13, the company is planning to unveil another batch of new products in the final week of the month. Here are the details.
New Macs and OLED iPad mini expected before year’s end

Over the weekend, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman claimed that Apple will, in fact, hold an event on October 13 to announce “its long-awaited smart home hub with a screen, the new HomePod mini and an updated Apple TV.”

Gurman’s report came amid uncertainty over whether Apple would hold an event or announce the new products through videos and press releases, as it has done in the past. Gurman had previously said only that Apple would unveil these products on October 13, without specifying how they would be announced.

In addition to these three products, Apple had also been expected to unveil a new OLED iPad mini and new Macs, including an updated iMac and a touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro, both powered by an M6 chip.
Now, MacRumors says that, “according to multiple sources familiar with the matter,” the company will unveil another round of new products in the final week of October.

The report stops short of saying which products will be announced. It also does not provide a specific date, or say whether Apple will hold a second event or unveil the products through videos and press releases.

That said, these announcements at the end of the month would cap off an unusually busy October for Apple, with the iPhone Duo launching on October 23 and the company also expected to report its quarterly results before the month is out.
What’s your take on Apple making a second round of product announcements later this month? Let us know in the comments.

All in all, it appears that Apple has two sets of product launches planned for this October, and that is on top of the iPhone Duo launching on Friday, October 23. Get ready, as it is about to be a busy couple of weeks in the world of Apple.

units.text: 快科技10月6日消息，2011年10月5日，苹果公司联合创始人史蒂夫·乔布斯因胰腺癌并发症去世，享年56岁。
在乔布斯逝世15周年之际，苹果CEO约翰·特努斯与苹果前CEO蒂姆·库克先后发文，缅怀这位苹果联合创始人。
特努斯表示：“Steve教会了我们用心对待每一个细节、每一份体验和每一个人，这份教益至今依然指引着我们的工作。永怀感激。”
库克则写道：“有的人在世界留下印记，而有的人彻底改变世界。Steve改变了世界，在这一过程中也改变了无数人的人生。毫无疑问，他永远改变了我的一生。他的精神长存于他所创造的一切之中，也长存在每一位受他启迪的人的心中。”
2007年，乔布斯发布第一代iPhone，以大尺寸多点触控屏幕和全新的交互逻辑重新定义了智能手机，并推动整个移动互联网产业进入新的发展阶段。
此后，iPhone、iPad、Mac等产品持续走向全球市场，苹果也逐渐构建起覆盖硬件、软件与服务的完整生态。
对于苹果而言，乔布斯留下的不只是几款划时代产品，更是一套延续至今的产品理念——对设计、体验和细节的极致追求。
15年过去，消费电子行业已经发生巨大变化，但乔布斯所推动的人机交互方式、产品设计理念以及软硬件融合思路，仍深刻影响着今天的科技产品。某种程度上，这也正是他留给苹果和整个行业最持久的遗产。
